run.help: Run a task or a script on one or more runners
run.help_long:
Sends your working tree as it is, with uncommitted changes and untracked files that Git doesn't
ignore, or the commit you name with --commit, and runs a task or a script there. Streams the
output while it runs and exits with the run's status. With several --os flags, runs one run per
operating system in parallel and exits with the first of these that applies:

1. 130, 141, or 143, when Proof canceled the runs: you pressed Ctrl-C, standard output was closed,
   or Proof received TERM.
2. The status of the first run whose command failed, or that someone else canceled, which counts as 130,
   in the order of the --os flags, not the order the runs finish. With --os all, the order is linux,
   macos, windows.
3. 78, when a run failed because of its artifacts: its command exited with 0 but Proof couldn't keep them, or the server was short of space and the command never started.
4. 75, when the pool failed, as when a runner's host went away.
5. 0.

A refusal, 2, comes before anything is sent, so it never mixes with these.

Proof's flags work anywhere before `--`. The words for the task follow `--`, as they do for
`cargo run` and `npm run`, and go to the task as they are, so they mean what they mean to mise. A
flag Proof doesn't have, before `--`, is a mistake: Proof names it, suggests the nearest flag it
has, and exits 2 without sending anything.

`:::` starts the next task, before or after `--`, as it does for `mise run`. The word after `:::`
is that task's name, and its words again follow `--`.

The words for a script follow `--` too, as in `proof run --script bench.sh -- --quick`, and go to
the script as its arguments, as `bash FILE ARGS` would pass them. A task and `--script` can't go
together: Proof refuses the line and exits 2.

Press Ctrl-C to cancel the run. To start a run without waiting for it, use --detach.
run.name: run

exit_codes.help: The run succeeded.
Proof refused the run before sending anything: the command line or the project file has a mistake, or no host has the resources the run requests.
A runner or its host went away, or Proof couldn't reach the server. Run the same command again.

The run failed because of its artifacts: its command exited with 0 but Proof couldn't keep them, because a --keep or artifact pattern matched no file or they exceeded the pool's limit; or the server was short of space, and the command never started.
The run reached its time limit, and the runner ended it.
The run was canceled: you interrupted Proof with Ctrl-C, or someone else, or the pool, canceled it. The result line says who canceled it.
The run held more memory than it requested while its host ran short, or was killed.
Standard output was closed, as by a pipe into head, and Proof canceled the run.
Proof received TERM, as when an agent harness stops it, and canceled the run.

setup.help: Set up this computer as a runner of the pool
setup.help_long:
Sets up this computer as a runner of the pool. Run it as the account the runner will run as: an
account set aside for Proof, not the account of anyone who uses the computer, and never root;
setup refuses to run as root. Prints a short code to approve with `proof runner approve`, so you
never type a long token at a text console. Where a step needs an administrator, such as adding
the account to the `kvm` group, setup prints the exact commands for you to run, and checks them
when you run setup again. On Windows, also sets up a runner in WSL. Safe to run again.

author: setdef
about: Run your project's tests and builds on your spare computers, from your working tree or any commit
about_long:
Proof sends your project from the computer you work on to the other Linux, Windows, and macOS
computers you have, runs its tests and builds there, streams their output back, and exits with
their status.

The task's output goes to standard output. The lines Proof prints go to standard error, and
each begins with "proof:".
